'''Richard Malcolm Sillitto''' (3 March 1923 &ndash; 19 April 2005) was an [[optics|optical]] [[physicist]] who wrote a useful text on [[quantum mechanics]]. He was a Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Edinburgh]] and Fellow of the Institute of Physics as well as a past president of the Scottish branch of the [[Institute of Physics]]. Sillitto was reader and Reader Emeritus in the physics department of the [[University of Edinburgh]].

Sillitto was born in [[Lockerbie]], the son of George Sillitto. He attended [[Dumfries Academy]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=1940-05-29 |title=Bursaries for Academy Pupils |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/dumfries-and-galloway-standard-bursaries/204158125/ |access-date=2026-08-19 |work=Dumfries and Galloway Standard |pages=4 |via=Newspapers.com}}</ref> During [[World War II]] he worked for the [[Admiralty Signals and Radar Establishment]] at [[Haslemere]]. After the war, he pursued advanced studies in optical physics at the University of Edinburgh.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |date=2005-05-06 |title=Obituary: Richard Sillitto |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/east-lothian-courier-obituary-richard-s/204157751/ |access-date=2026-08-19 |work=East Lothian Courier |pages=15 |via=Newspapers.com}}</ref>

Sillitto married Winifred McMillan, an engineer, in 1947.<ref>{{Cite news |date=1947-09-18 |title=Sillitto-McMillan |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/belfast-telegraph-sillitto-mcmillan/204158383/ |access-date=2026-08-19 |work=Belfast Telegraph |pages=1 |via=Newspapers.com}}</ref> They had a son. Sillitto died in [[Dunbar]] in 2005, at the age of 82.<ref name=":0" />
